title: Expected cost of a distribution
statement: Let $\beta$ be a type and let $p$ be a probability distribution on pairs consisting of an element of $\beta$ and a natural-number cost. Its expected cost is the sum over all outcomes of the probability of the outcome multiplied by its cost, as an extended nonnegative real number.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a probability distribution on $\beta\times\mathbb N$
